[Rating: 1/10] So disappointed that I didn't pay more attention when buying this. I never would have bought it if I'd realized it has (crappy - look at the architecture in the background) AI art. And Unigoat Edition's comments on here and BGA about how the "artist" trained an AI model based entirely on his own work is either remarkably naive if they were told that and believe it, or a botched PR attempt that's a direct insult to players. I wish I could get a refund, but at minimum I'd like to see it removed from BGA and for the creators to stop doubling down on such obvious lies.

[Rating: 1/10] :thumbsdown: AI "Art"  Unethically sourced artwork,  brought to you by immoral tech bros,  generated by creative hacks,  platformed and promoted by greedy publishers,  for ignorant consumers

[Rating: 1/10] Played once on bga for bga's "summer of games" at 2 players. I'm comfortable saying that it's terrible. The summer of games being branded as cat-themed was sorta weird to start, but this is an amusing punchline. -It drags badly. It just doesn't need to last this long. -the iconography might as well have been picked out of a hat. Without the bga tooltips this would have been pretty annoying for such a light game. -There's not much strategy, which is fine for a game like this that's just trying to be cute and light, but if that's the idea then it needs to not take so long, and actually be cute. 

[Rating: 1/10] The AI Artwork is extremely off-putting.  It is not disclosed on the outside of the box that it uses AI Artwork.  It is a terrible development for the board game industry. Physical Board Games was one place I thought was safe from AI Art.  There are so many games out there with gorgeous artwork by real artists. It is a big part of the experience of man games. But I'd rather play the ugliest bare bones protoype than a game than games that use AI "art"

[Rating: 1/10] Played on BGA. Ignored the terrible A.I. art and tried to just play it.  It's an awful luck based game in which you have little to no choices. If your opponent is lucky enough to have pairs of the cards you play, you can do absolutely nothing to counter.  No doubt one could use the same LLM that was used to create the art to create a bot to play it with the same success of a human player.  Fun Fact: By the time I wrote this review, 80% of the high game ratings (7 to 10) were given by users of Quebec, Canada, same as the designer. Coincidence?

[Rating: 1/10] counter balancing the AI generated art + the 10 from the designer/"artist" itself asking for more boosters.  Growth hacking has certain limits with honesty/humility.

[Rating: 1/10] Based mostly on luck, more of the same.  I lowered my rating from 2 to 1 after seeing all those fake reviews giving high ratings.

[Rating: 2/10] Not a fan of team games anyway, but this game defies the definition with so little interaction between teammates (there are 2 "teamwork" cards in the entire deck). It basically plays itself - play a card if it happens to match the number of the last played card or has an effect where you meet the condition, that's it. Save counter cards until you need them.  The end game is pointless, as once your hand size starts decreasing, it's unlikely you can do anything. [Rating: 2/10] AI art aside, is this a good game? I would say no. It is super swingy depending on if you have the right cards in your hand and there are not often interesting choices.  I think it could have a place with younger kids. I'd compare it to the back-and-forth grind of a card game like War but with a cute cat theme.  The AI art just cements it in the 'bad game' category. I'd like to see human art in board games.
